tasks.title: Stamp brief-derived metadata (working_dir, required_task_ids) onto the plan BEFORE validate_plan
acceptance_criteria: harness/planner/cli.py defines a new module-level helper `_stamp_brief_metadata(plan, brief_obj)` placed just above `persist_plan`, with the exact docstring and body specified in the brief (idempotent, never overwrites an existing key, returns plan unchanged when brief_obj is None or plan is not a dict).

In `main()`, a call `_stamp_brief_metadata(final_plan, brief_obj)` is inserted IMMEDIATELY AFTER the `final_plan = normalize_plan(...)` line and BEFORE the `from harness.planner.plan_validator import validate_plan` import / `validate_plan(final_plan)` call.

The rest of harness/planner/cli.py is reproduced byte-for-byte; `persist_plan`, `validate_plan`, and all other functions are unchanged; the file still ends with `if __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()`.
A new GREEN test file tests/planner/test_stamp_brief_metadata.py exists with at least 4 concrete test functions (no trivial/assert True) and is hermetic (no planner run, no network).
Both files are delivered via a single `__JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__` containing the WHOLE content of both files; no `__JANUSMASK_PATCHES__` is emitted.
`python -m pytest tests/planner/test_stamp_brief_metadata.py -q` passes and no file other than the two listed is changed.

spec.objective: Fix a regression from b84f635 (validate-before-persist): brief-derived metadata (plan['working_dir'], plan['required_task_ids'], source_brief_path/sha256, parent_epic_slug) was stamped only inside persist_plan(), which now runs AFTER validate_plan(). As a result the validator sees working_dir=None, so plan_validator._is_module_creating resolves external-working_dir EDIT leaves against the wrong root (the JanusMask repo) and falsely flags them module-creating, raising a spurious PlanViolation('missing_wiring_oracle') that makes every external EDIT leaf fail to plan; it also leaves required_task_ids=None at validation time, making missing_required_task enforcement inert. The fix introduces an idempotent helper `_stamp_brief_metadata` and calls it in main() BEFORE validate_plan so the validator sees working_dir and required_task_ids.
functional_requirements: Add a module-level helper `_stamp_brief_metadata(plan, brief_obj)` to harness/planner/cli.py, placed just above `persist_plan`, that idempotently stamps source_brief_path, source_brief_sha256, working_dir, required_task_ids, and parent_epic_slug onto the plan dict, guarding each write with `'<key>' not in plan` so an existing key is never overwritten.

The helper must short-circuit and return `plan` unchanged when `brief_obj is None` or `plan` is not a dict, and must read brief attributes defensively via getattr (source_path, sha256, working_dir, required_task_ids defaulting to (), parent_epic_slug), coercing required_task_ids to `list(rti)` only when it is a non-empty list/tuple.

In `main()`, insert `_stamp_brief_metadata(final_plan, brief_obj)` immediately after the `final_plan = normalize_plan(final_plan, repo_root=_effective_repo_root(brief_obj))` line and before the `from harness.planner.plan_validator import validate_plan` import and `validate_plan(final_plan)` call, so the validator sees working_dir + required_task_ids.

Reproduce the entire rest of harness/planner/cli.py verbatim: do NOT modify `persist_plan` (its existing idempotent stamping block stays, now harmlessly redundant for these keys), `validate_plan`, `normalize_plan`, or any other function; the file still ends with `if __name__ == '__main__':` then `    main()`.

Create the new hermetic test tests/planner/test_stamp_brief_metadata.py importing `_stamp_brief_metadata` from `harness.planner.cli`, using a SimpleNamespace/small-class stand-in brief, with at least 4 concrete behavior tests including the validate_plan integration-intent assertion that an EXISTING-file harness_self_fix EDIT leaf with working_dir='.' yields no `missing_wiring_oracle` violation.

Deliver both files through a single `__JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__` whole-file payload (not `__JANUSMASK_PATCHES__`), keeping all docstrings as triple-double-quote and emitting no backslash-escaped or single-triple-quote strings inside file bodies.
spec.interfaces: harness/planner/cli.py: NEW module-level `def _stamp_brief_metadata(plan, brief_obj)` returning the (mutated) plan; CHANGED `main()` gains one call `_stamp_brief_metadata(final_plan, brief_obj)` between `normalize_plan(...)` and the `validate_plan` import/call. UNCHANGED: `persist_plan(plan, out_path, brief_obj=None)` keeps its idempotent stamping block; `validate_plan` reads `plan.get('working_dir')` and passes it to `plan_validator._is_module_creating(..., working_dir=wd)`. New test module imports `_stamp_brief_metadata` and `harness.planner.plan_validator.validate_plan`.
edge_cases: brief_obj is None -> helper returns plan unchanged, no crash, no keys added.
plan is not a dict -> helper returns it unchanged.

plan already has working_dir (e.g. 'X') -> NOT overwritten by the brief's value (idempotence); same guard for every stamped key so calling the helper then persist_plan's own stamping is a no-op for these keys.
required_task_ids is None or empty tuple -> not stamped; when a non-empty list/tuple it is coerced via list(rti).
Brief attributes missing entirely (getattr defaults) -> only present, correctly-typed values are stamped.
Calling the helper twice is a no-op the second time (idempotent).
non_goals: INTEGRATION beyond these two files is out of scope: do NOT edit plan_validator.py, plan_normalizer.py, persist_plan's stamping block, blind_draft.py, or any other file.
Do not decompose into multiple tasks or emit __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__.
Do not change validate_plan, normalize_plan, or persist_plan behavior.
No integration test that runs the full planner end-to-end, spawns a subprocess, or touches the network.
spec.implementation_notes: Single task delivering BOTH files via one `__JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__` (whole-file content of harness/planner/cli.py reproduced verbatim with exactly the two additive changes, plus the new test). OMIT mutation_target (this is harness_self_fix, not test_authoring). READ harness/planner/cli.py first and copy it byte-for-byte except: (1) add `_stamp_brief_metadata` just above `persist_plan` with the exact body from the brief; (2) add the single `_stamp_brief_metadata(final_plan, brief_obj)` call after `normalize_plan(...)` and before the `validate_plan` import. Author the test GREEN: assert `_stamp_brief_metadata({}, brief)` sets plan['working_dir'] to the brief's working_dir and plan['required_task_ids'] to list(brief.required_task_ids); assert a plan already carrying working_dir='X' is not overwritten; assert `_stamp_brief_metadata(plan, None)` returns the plan unchanged; and assert the integration intent that a one-task plan whose only task has files_touched=['harness/planner/cli.py'] and meta_task_type='harness_self_fix', after stamping with a brief whose working_dir='.', produces no `missing_wiring_oracle` violation from validate_plan. Keep all docstrings as triple-double-quote; do not emit single-triple-quote or backslash-escaped quotes inside file bodies.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: A tiny stand-in brief object via types.SimpleNamespace (or a small class) carrying attributes working_dir, required_task_ids, source_path, sha256, parent_epic_slug. A plan dict containing exactly one task whose files_touched=['harness/planner/cli.py'] (an EXISTING repo file) and meta_task_type='harness_self_fix', stamped with a brief whose working_dir='.' so cli.py resolves as an existing file. No fixtures requiring network, subprocess, or a full planner run.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is mostly verbatim reproduction of cli.py plus two small additive changes; the bulk of net-new authored logic is the GREEN regression test, so test tokens dominate (>= 1.5x implementation tokens).
